claims.text: Conventionally synthesized multi-element, near-equiatomic solid-solution nanoparticles have heterogeneous size distributions.
Conventionally synthesized multi-element, near-equiatomic solid-solution nanoparticles have variable surface-ligand chemistries.
Controlled nucleation and growth protocols can produce a uniform, small nanoparticle-size distribution.
Defined, robust capping ligands stabilize nanoparticle surfaces.
A narrow, small-size distribution and robust surface capping improve structural stability under high-temperature catalytic and thermoelectric conditions.
A narrow, small-size distribution and robust surface capping improve chemical stability under high-temperature catalytic and thermoelectric conditions.
Controlled nanoparticle size reduces surface-energy-driven phase separation.
Stable surface chemistry reduces chemical segregation.
A narrow size distribution and stable ligand capping reduce nanoparticle surface energy.
Reduced surface energy minimizes the thermodynamic driving force for phase separation at elevated temperature.
Reduced surface energy minimizes the thermodynamic driving force for chemical segregation at elevated temperature.
Nanoparticles with broad size distributions and less effective surface capping are more prone to coarsening under high-temperature service.
Nanoparticles with broad size distributions and less effective surface capping are more prone to degradation under high-temperature service.
Controlled-size, defined-ligand nanoparticles will retain a single-phase structure during prolonged high-temperature exposure.
Controlled-size, defined-ligand nanoparticles will retain a homogeneous elemental distribution during prolonged high-temperature exposure.
Conventionally synthesized nanoparticles will develop measurable phase separation during prolonged high-temperature exposure.
Conventionally synthesized nanoparticles will develop measurable chemical inhomogeneity during prolonged high-temperature exposure.
The proposed stabilization effect may not apply to markedly non-equiatomic systems, pure metals, or nanoparticles dominated by other stabilization mechanisms.
